title: Ang 1312–1318: Kanara ki Var and Namdev
hookLine: the ballad and a Bhagat's hymn
tomorrow: the goodbye dinner. what does her dad finally say?

cards: Six in the morning, and Simran is at the mirror in the hallway, pinning her chunni for the gurdwara goodbye on Sunday, taking it off, pinning it again. Her phone sits on the shelf below.
She sent her one line to the guy from the group chat last night: that joke landed on real people; happy to explain anything about Sikhi sometime. No reply yet.
She looks at her own face, a little puffy from not sleeping, and wonders what his looks like right now. Namdev looked in a mirror once, too, and saw something else.

teach.h: KANARA KI VAR: THE NIGHT BALLAD.
teach.b: First, the ballad. Kanara ki Var, Guru Ram Das's ballad in the night raga, begins on ang 1312: pauris with saloks before them, the same build as the ballads in Sarang and Malar.

teach.h: NAMDEV: A FACE IN A MIRROR.
teach.b: Then, as the raga closes on ang 1318, Namdev has a short hymn, and it's a mirror. In paraphrase: the Sovereign who knows every heart is like a face seen in a mirror.
He lives in each and every heart, and nothing sticks to him. Look at what the picture does. A face in a mirror is fully there, and you can't touch it.
Put a mirror in every room of the house, and the same face is in all of them at once. Smudge the glass, and the face isn't smudged.

teach.h: IN EVERY HEART, STAINED BY NOTHING.
teach.b: Namdev's One is in every heart like that: present everywhere, stained by nothing the heart gets up to.

teach.h: THE SAME FACE IN EVERYONE'S GLASS.
teach.b: Here's something to tell a friend tonight: in Namdev's mirror, the face that shows up in every glass isn't yours. It's the One's, and it's in everyone's. Even the hallway glass of a guy who made a bad joke.
Simran stops fiddling with the pin. The chunni sits a little crooked. She leaves it.

how: Kanara ki Var is sung in kirtan pauri by pauri with its saloks; Namdev's mirror hymn is found under his name at the end of raga Kanara.

o: where Guru Arjan says no one is a stranger
where Guru Nanak opens the dawn raga
where Guru Ram Das's ballad in the night raga begins

games.q: the end of the night raga — tap the pairs.
p: Guru Ram Das's ballad in the night raga
a face seen in a mirror
stained by nothing the heart does

s: Namdev says the One in each heart is stained by what the heart does
nothing sticks to him, the hymn says: in every heart, and untouched.
Kanara ki Var, like the ballads in Sarang and Malar, sets saloks before its pauris
the same build: stanzas, with short verses before them.
Namdev's mirror hymn is a portrait of what God looks like
it's a picture of presence: one face showing in every glass at once.

games.q: a seven-year-old at the gurdwara asks how God can be inside everybody at the same time. with Namdev's hymn in mind, what do you show her?
o: a mirror: one face, showing in every glass, smudged by none.
a photo: God looks one way, and each of us carries a copy.
a puzzle: everyone holds a tiny piece, and nobody has much.
games.why: Namdev: the One who knows every heart is like a face in a mirror, living in each heart, with nothing sticking to him.

practice: If you can, look into a window or a dark phone screen and find your face there. Don't fix anything. Let your eyes rest on it the way you'd look at someone you love, breathing slowly, and then let your gaze go soft.

carryVoice: The line for the road: the ballad, and a mirror where the same face shows in every heart. Day sixteen hundred seven.
